Description: One of Delhi's oldest churches, built in Renaissance Neo-Classical cross layout. Citations: William Dalrymple (2006), 'The Last Mughal'; Swapna Liddle (2018), 'Delhi: 14 Historic Walks'.
Gothic spire on Northern Ridge commemorating soldiers from the 1857 siege. Citations: William Dalrymple (2006), 'The Last Mughal'; Christopher Hibbert (1978), 'The Great Mutiny: India 1857'.

Open ground used for three Imperial Durbars (1877, 1903, 1911). Citations: Robert Irving (1981), 'Indian Summer: Lutyens, Baker, and Imperial Delhi'; Narayani Gupta (1981), 'Delhi Between Two Empires 1803-1931'.

Originally Viceroy's House; Neo-Classical palace with Buddhist/Indian motifs. Citations: Robert Irving (1981), 'Indian Summer: Lutyens, Baker, and Imperial Delhi'; Christopher Hussey (1950), 'The Life of Sir Edwin Lutyens'.

Colonnaded circular sandstone building inspired by Chausath Yogini Temple. Citations: Robert Irving (1981), 'Indian Summer: Lutyens, Baker, and Imperial Delhi'; Narayani Gupta (1981), 'Delhi Between Two Empires'.

42m-high war memorial arch honoring Commonwealth soldiers from WWI. Citations: Robert Irving (1981), 'Indian Summer: Lutyens, Baker, and Imperial Delhi'; Gavin Stamp (2002), 'The Memorial to the Missing of the Somme'.
